title: Transaction with 100 operations, 20 used signatures and a 28-byte text memo
caps_note: The bounds (100 operations, 20 signatures, 28-byte memo text) are fixed by the XDR definitions and stellar-core constants in every protocol; no CAP introduced them.
why: Each of the three vectors is at its maximum at once: 100 operations, 20 signatures from 20 accounts and a 28-byte memo. Readers with fixed buffers, a lower operation cap or a row per signature limit drop operations, signatures or memo bytes, and a 100-movement transaction exposes per-transaction batching limits.

values.note: The hundredth operation, the most one transaction may carry (MAX_OPS_PER_TX).
First of 20 signatures, the most an envelope may carry: S00's (hint = last 4 bytes of its key).
The twentieth signature, S19's. Every one is used: each account signs only for its own five operations.
A text memo of exactly 28 bytes, the maximum.
100 operations at the base fee of 100 stroops; the bid was 20000.
The text memo is copied into every payment event as to_muxed_id; it is the sender's text, not an address.

notes: Generated by xdrcheck-corpus gen from scenarios/s11-maximum-length-vectors.yaml on a local stellar-core, at Protocols 28 and 30 on the testnet and public passphrases (four variants); the accounts are label-derived and equal across variants, hashes are per variant under derived. Each of the 20 accounts is the source of five payments and signs only for its own key, because stellar-core refuses a signature it did not need (txBAD_AUTH_EXTRA). The fee is 100 operations at the base fee (10000) against a bid of 20000. Every payment event carries the text memo as to_muxed_id; the movements list all 100 with that routing. No reader has been run against these ledgers yet, so the entry lists no known divergence. Replay is by chain; serving the ledger alone has not been tried.
